summary: The opt-in source-feasibility helper demonstrates bounded pipe/gzip byte capture and strict single-member decoding, with synthetic FD controls. It is not called by command profiles and does not select a new trace format or qualification ordinal. Current strace -ff opens per-PID paths directly, whereas a source-owned streaming encoder needs an explicit inherited-FD/framing contract and bounded multiplexing with readiness, original clocks, accounting and owned actor retirement. Post-hoc compression does not prevent raw live quota exhaustion. Codec-owned byte accounting is not complete physical namespace custody: canonical names, retained capabilities, all artifacts and manifest-time drift checks remain to be joined. Decoded callbacks are provisional until complete success, and byte identity alone is not trusted-source or semantic read/lifetime acceptance. The existing Execution/PROC owner must supply the joined producer/parser/custody design under root selection before live support. Current raw profile, fresh drift observations, full trace semantics and maximum qualification ordinal4 remain unchanged. Source controls do not establish full-stream fit or native/runtime acceptance.
title: A lossless source codec does not supply the joined PROC trace producer
